Command: Do not eat flesh torn by beasts
Summary: Flesh torn by beasts in the field may not be eaten; as holy men, Israel shall cast it to the dogs instead.
Commandment: Do not eat flesh torn of beasts in the field; cast it to the dogs.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The rule kept Israel from eating an animal killed and mauled rather than slaughtered, and it is classed here with the food laws rather than with the civil restitution laws of its parent row. The New Testament records the food distinctions set aside (Mark 7:19; Acts 10).
Purpose: Scripture's stated context: ye shall be holy men unto me, and shall not eat flesh torn of beasts (Exodus 22:31).
